context: a letter from J. D. Hooker, which you are answering
exchanges:
from him pæans of praise till I struck him down with a criticism on Ungers letter to him, & I believe caused the cancelling of sundry pages of Siluria— I will find his letter & shew it you— I was bound to keep the thing a profound secret till Siluria appeared: in fact Murchy is always exciting my contempt—it is very wrong of me I dare say, & indeed I believe all you say in his praise as a truly great geologist, but I beg permission to believe it as a superstition received from you & hope not to have the articles of my creed enquired into.

I was mistaken about the Greenland Flora; there is none but I have just received all Lyalls Arctic collections & am going to draw up a Geograph: Bot: account of the Greenland & Polar sea plants

Three of the Marianne Islds were visited by Freycinet, & a rather long acct of them is in Gaudichauds account of the Botany of the Voyage

I have not yet reworked the question of aberrant genera, but have not lost sight of it.

I have a glorious fact for you— A tropical species of Cyperus (polystachyus) & a tropical Fern, Pteris longifolia, grow in the hot soil of the volcano of Ischia & no where else in Europe or the Mediterr: see Hookers Jour. Bot for Nov 1854. p. 351. (it is on Athenæum table—) now I can wriggle out of the Fern case by allowing ubiquitous meteroric dispersion of Fern spores, but the Cyperus is a disgusting & detestable fact, that disquiets my soul within me. I must however have a bite at you if I can & so will ask why if the Cyperus & Pteris got there no other migrators did?—

Can you come to Linn. Soc. on Tuesday evening at 8 for a few minutes: it is the first meeting & would please Bell amazingly.

We had a superb drive to the C. Palace & never enjoyed anything more than the scenery & foliage. The C. P. too was paradisaical & thoroughly enjoyable. We both of us said we had not spent 5 happier days since our marriage.

Ever yours | J D Hooker

I am glad to hear about Greenland.

What a disgusting puzzle about your Ischian case. I have begun to get some facts about aberrant genera in insects.—

I cannot possibly come up on Tuesday, as we shall have visitors; whether I shd. if we had not, shall be left in obscurity.
